messages:
Ingrid: FYI incident-bot is spamming pager for tokenizer-error-rate in region-eu — ~60 alerts in 10m. Looks correlated with the model swap we rolled at 22:40 UTC. Not a customer outage but noise is drowning real pages. I'm handing off early — need a fast decision on temporary suppression / threshold change. Primary right now is Pat, secondary Maya.

rotation-bot: Pat is scheduled primary until 23:30 UTC. Maya is listed as secondary.

Pat: I have to step out at 23:05 (family thing). I can stay on for a hard handoff for 10m but prefer Maya take primary if possible.

Maya: I can take primary at 23:00. Will monitor. Can you list the exact alert rule to suppress?

Ingrid: Rule name `alert:tokenizer-errored-rate` (alerts on >2% error-rate over 5m). Proposal: raise alert threshold to 4% for 60m and apply suppression to avoid duplicate pagers while we investigate the model variant mismatch. No evidence of customer-facing failures — only internal decoder errors that are retried.

Sam: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tokenizer-errors (see Mitigation -> Temporary threshold). Suggested commands (Grafana alert-manager / opsctl):

```
# temporary suppression via opsctl
opsctl suppress --rule alert:tokenizer-errored-rate --until 2026-03-15T05:00:00Z --reason "model swap noise; night handoff" --owner Maya

# or update Prometheus alert rule (quick patch)
kubectl -n monitoring patch configmap alerts --patch '{"data":{"tokenizer_rule_threshold":"4"}}'
```

Maya: I'll take owner and apply suppression. Will also post a checkpoint in the incident ticket with the exact command.

incident-bot: Pager summary: 63 alerts, region=eu, peak=22:48 UTC, average-error-rate=2.9%, retries=0.92 avg. Linked runbook: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0314-12

Pat: If you suppress, please also add a short-lived augmentation to the alert (reason + owner) so rotations know it's intentional. I'll create a short ticket when I'm back online.

Maya: Applying suppression now. Command: `opsctl suppress --rule alert:tokenizer-errored-rate --until 2026-03-15T05:00:00Z --reason "model-swap noise; nightshift mute" --owner Maya`

Ingrid: Confirmed suppression entry in alert-manager (ID sup-20260314-7). Also bumped threshold in the config to 4% for 60m. Leaving a note on the runbook to revert at 05:00 UTC unless we see real customer signals.

Maya: Monitoring charts — spikes dropping after suppression; 5xxs for customers remain at baseline. No PagerDuty escalations expected. I'll be primary until 05:00 UTC per this change. Pat — enjoy the family time, ping if you want a short sync later. :thumbsup:

Pat: Thanks all. Quick SLO note for the log: temporary alert tuning increases detection latency for this class of errors; we've documented potential SLA implications in the ticket (very low risk for customers).

Ingrid: Filed ops-ticket OPS-4721 with tags `oncall-handoff`, `temp-suppression`, `slo-impact`. Revert reminder set: 2026-03-15T05:00:00Z.

Maya: Leaving a short checklist for whoever picks this back up: 1) validate tokenization success on a sample traffic stream, 2) revert threshold + clear suppression, 3) run postmortem if counts > baseline after revert.

rotation-bot: Handoff note: Primary now Maya (until 05:00 UTC). Secondary unassigned — please update if you pick up backup.

incident-bot: Incident closed (noise mitigated). Total noise pages suppressed: 59.

Ingrid: Post-handoff note: we should add a small automation to auto-suggest suppression when >30 similar alerts from same model-swap within 10m — reduces noisy pages during controlled rollouts. Filing engineering follow-up.
